source.text: μιμηταί μου γίνεσθε, καθὼς κἀγὼ Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Imitators of me become, just as I also of Christ.

en.L: Become imitators of me, just as I also [am] of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: Take me as your model, just as I take {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} as mine.
en.R: Copy the way I live, just as I copy the way {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} lived.

fr.L: Devenez mes imitateurs, comme moi aussi [je le suis] du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Prenez-moi pour modèle, comme je prends moi-même le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} pour modèle.
fr.R: Imitez ma façon de vivre, comme j’imite la façon dont le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} a vécu.

es.L: {{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} imitadores míos, así como yo también [lo soy] de {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Tómenme|Tomadme}} como modelo, así como yo tomo como modelo {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Imiten|Imitad}} mi manera de vivir, así como yo imito la manera en que vivió {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}.

decisions.choice: this sentence closes the argument of chapters 8-10, and does not open the new section
alternatives: the first sentence of the instructions on worship in chapter 11
decisions.reason: The chapter divisions were added to the text more than a thousand years after Paul wrote. 10:31-33 ends with Paul's own example: he seeks not his own good but the good of the many, so that they may be saved. "Imitate me" sums that up, and 11:2 then begins a new subject with a fresh opening, Ἐπαινῶ δὲ ("now I praise"), where the SBLGNT starts a new paragraph.

decisions.choice: imitate Paul as he imitates Christ: follow his example of giving up his own rights for the good of others, as Christ did
decisions.reason: μιμητής is one who copies another's way of life (4:16; Philippians 3:17). The example Paul means is the one he has just described in 9:19-23 and 10:33. He asks to be followed only so far as he follows Christ, whose self-giving is the pattern (Romans 15:2-3; Philippians 2:4-8).

decisions.choice: Take me as your model (B); Copy the way I live (R)
decisions.reason: "Imitators" is stiff in ordinary speech, so Balanced and Readable say what imitating means. Literal keeps the noun, as at 4:16.

decisions.choice: the way {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} lived
decisions.reason: Readable completes the short comparison ("as I of Christ") so that it reads as a full sentence (m2).

decisions.choice: "du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}", "le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}", with the article outside the span (for chapters 11-13)
decisions.reason: French needs the article with "Messie", and "le Christ" reads naturally beside it, so the article stays outside the span and both options read as French. "In Christ" is "{{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}", as in Colossians.

decisions.choice: [lo soy] de {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}
decisions.reason: Spanish needs the verb that the Greek leaves out, so Literal supplies "[lo soy]". The alternative keeps the article Spanish needs before "Mesías".

source.text: Ἐπαινῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς ὅτι πάντα μου μέμνησθε καὶ καθὼς παρέδωκα ὑμῖν τὰς παραδόσεις κατέχετε.

records.literal_gloss: I praise but you that all things of me you remember and just as I handed on to you the traditions you hold fast.

en.L: Now I praise you because you remember me in all things and hold fast the traditions just as I handed [them] on to you.
en.B: I praise you, because you keep me in mind in everything, and you hold firmly to the traditions in the form I passed them on to you.
en.R: I praise you, because you remember me in every way, and you keep to the teachings I passed on to you, just as I gave them.

fr.L: Or je vous loue de ce que vous vous souvenez de moi en toutes choses et de ce que vous retenez les traditions telles que je vous [les] ai transmises.
fr.B: Je vous félicite de ce que vous pensez à moi en tout et de ce que vous gardez fermement les traditions telles que je vous les ai transmises.
fr.R: Je vous félicite, parce que vous vous souvenez de moi en tout et que vous restez fidèles aux enseignements que je vous ai transmis, tels que je vous les ai donnés.

es.L: Ahora bien, {{plural_you:los|os}} alabo porque en todo se {{plural_you:acuerdan|acordáis}} de mí y {{plural_you:retienen|retenéis}} las tradiciones tal como {{plural_you:se las|os las}} entregué.
es.B: {{plural_you:Los|Os}} alabo, porque en todo me {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} presente, y {{plural_you:se mantienen|os mantenéis}} firmes en las tradiciones tal como {{plural_you:se las|os las}} transmití.
es.R: {{plural_you:Los|Os}} alabo, porque se {{plural_you:acuerdan|acordáis}} de mí en todo, y {{plural_you:siguen|seguís}} las enseñanzas que {{plural_you:les|os}} transmití, tal como {{plural_you:se las|os las}} di.

decisions.choice: traditions: the teaching about Christ and the practices of the churches, which Paul received and passed on
decisions.reason: παραδόσεις means what is handed on. Paul uses the same pair of verbs, "hand on" (παρέδωκα) and "receive", for the Lord's Supper in 11:23 and for the gospel in 15:3: what he passes on is not his own invention. Here the word is good; in Colossians 2:8 and Galatians 1:14 it is used of merely human tradition.

decisions.choice: remember me in all things: keep Paul and his teaching in mind in every respect
decisions.reason: πάντα ("all things") says in what respect they remember him. The praise is real but general; it sets up the correction that follows, and stands against "I do not praise you" in 11:17 and 11:22.

decisions.choice: teachings
decisions.reason: "Traditions" can suggest old customs kept out of habit; Readable says plainly that Paul means what he taught them (m1). Literal and Balanced keep "traditions".

decisions.choice: je vous loue (L); je vous félicite (B, R) (also in verses 17 and 22)
alternatives: je vous loue at every level
decisions.reason: "Louer" said of people sounds old-fashioned and is mostly kept for praising God in modern French. Balanced and Readable use "féliciter", the ordinary word for praising people for what they do; the same verb returns in verses 17 and 22, so the link Paul makes between them stays visible.

decisions.choice: tradiciones (L, B); enseñanzas (R)
decisions.reason: The word is the teaching and practice Paul received and passed on (m1). "Tradiciones" keeps the Greek word, without the sense of mere human custom; Readable says "enseñanzas", as the English says "teachings".

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:los|os}} alabo
decisions.reason: Spanish "alabar" is used for praising people as well as God, and is kept through the chapter (verses 17 and 22), so the reader hears verse 22 look back to verse 2.

source.text: θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς εἰδέναι ὅτι παντὸς ἀνδρὸς ἡ κεφαλὴ ὁ Χριστός ἐστιν, κεφαλὴ δὲ γυναικὸς ὁ ἀνήρ, κεφαλὴ δὲ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὁ θεός.

records.literal_gloss: I want but you to know that of every man the head the Christ is, head but of woman the man, head but of the Christ the God.

en.L: But I want you to know that the head of every man is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, and [the] head of a woman [is] the man, and [the] head of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} [is] God.
en.B: But there is something I want you to understand: {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is the head of every man, man is the head of woman, and God is the head of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: I want you to understand this. {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} is the head of every man. Man is the head of woman. And God is the head of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

fr.L: Mais je veux que vous sachiez que la tête de tout homme est le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, que la tête de la femme [est] l’homme, et que la tête du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} [est] Dieu.
fr.B: Mais il y a une chose que je veux vous faire comprendre : le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est la tête de tout homme, l’homme est la tête de la femme, et Dieu est la tête du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.R: Je veux que vous compreniez ceci. Le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est la tête de tout homme. L’homme est la tête de la femme. Et Dieu est la tête du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.

es.L: Pero quiero que {{plural_you:sepan|sepáis}} que la cabeza de todo hombre es el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, y [la] cabeza de la mujer [es] el hombre, y [la] cabeza del {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} [es] Dios.
es.B: Pero hay algo que quiero que {{plural_you:entiendan|entendáis}}: {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} es la cabeza de todo hombre, el hombre es la cabeza de la mujer, y Dios es la cabeza {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}.
es.R: Quiero que {{plural_you:entiendan|entendáis}} esto. {{christos:Cristo|El Mesías}} es la cabeza de todo hombre. El hombre es la cabeza de la mujer. Y Dios es la cabeza {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}.

decisions.choice: head: the one who has the place of leadership and authority in a relationship, here in relationships where the two are not unequal in worth, since God is the head of Christ
alternatives: head: source or origin, as the head of a river, so that man is the source of woman (verses 8 and 12) and God the one from whom Christ comes
head: the most prominent or honored member, whose honor the other reflects
decisions.reason: κεφαλή is the head of a body; used of a person it is a picture, and the picture must be read from its uses. In the Greek Old Testament it often stands for a leader or ruler of a people (Judges 11:11; 2 Samuel 22:44), and in Paul's letters Christ is "head over all things" (Ephesians 1:22) and "head of every ruler and authority" (Colossians 2:10), where leadership and rule are the point. The sense "source" is also found in Greek, and verses 8 and 12, where woman comes from man and all things from God, give it support; Colossians 2:19 and Ephesians 4:15-16 also picture the body drawing its life from the head. "The head of Christ is God" shows that headship here does not mean lesser worth or a lesser nature: Christ is head of every man, and God of Christ, within one order. The evidence is debated, and both senses are well represented in careful readings.

decisions.choice: man ... woman: men and women in general, not husbands and wives only
alternatives: husband ... wife: "the head of a wife is her husband"
decisions.reason: ἀνήρ and γυνή mean both "man" and "husband", "woman" and "wife"; only the context decides. Verses 4-5 speak of "every man" and "every woman" who prays or prophesies, and verses 7-9 and 12 argue from the creation of the first man and woman, which points to men and women in general. But in that world a married woman's head covering marked her as a wife in public, so Paul may have married women most in mind, and "husband" suits the second clause well, as in Ephesians 5:23. The same choice is made through verse 16.

decisions.choice: I want you to know: new teaching, set beside the traditions they already keep (verse 2)
decisions.reason: After praising them for holding to what he passed on, Paul adds something they have not yet grasped. δὲ ("but") marks the turn.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is the head of every man, man is the head of woman, and God is the head of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}
alternatives: the head of every man is {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put each subject first, which reads more easily as a list of three. Literal keeps the Greek order, with "head" first each time. All three keep "head" without explaining it, since its sense is debated (m1).

decisions.choice: la tête
decisions.reason: "Le chef" would settle the sense of "head", which is debated (m1), and "la source" would settle it the other way. "La tête" keeps Paul's image at every level, as the English "head" does, and French already uses it for the one who is at the head of something. "Homme" and "femme" here mean men and women, not human beings in general, so they take no gender setting.

decisions.choice: cabeza
decisions.reason: Spanish "cabeza" also means the one who leads ("cabeza de familia"), as the meaning decision reads it (m1, footnoted), so every level keeps the Greek picture, which verses 4-7 turn on.

decisions.choice: hombre, mujer
decisions.reason: The words mean men and women in general (m2), so every level says "hombre" and "mujer", not "marido" and "esposa" as in chapter 7; "hombre" here is a male, so it takes no gender setting.

source.text: πᾶς ἀνὴρ προσευχόμενος ἢ προφητεύων κατὰ κεφαλῆς ἔχων καταισχύνει τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: Every man praying or prophesying down from head having dishonors the head of him;

en.L: Every man praying or prophesying having [something] down from [his] head dishonors his head;
en.B: Any man who prays or prophesies with something covering his head brings shame on his head.
en.R: If a man prays or prophesies, speaking a message from God, with something covering his head, he brings shame on his head.

fr.L: Tout homme qui prie ou prophétise en ayant [quelque chose] qui pend de la tête déshonore sa tête ;
fr.B: Tout homme qui prie ou prophétise la tête couverte fait honte à sa tête.
fr.R: Si un homme prie ou prophétise, c’est-à-dire s’il transmet un message de Dieu, avec quelque chose sur la tête, il fait honte à sa tête.

es.L: Todo hombre que ora o profetiza teniendo [algo] que le cuelga de la cabeza, deshonra su cabeza;
es.B: Todo hombre que ora o profetiza con algo que le cubre la cabeza, avergüenza a su cabeza.
es.R: Si un hombre ora o profetiza, comunicando un mensaje de parte de Dios, con algo que le cubre la cabeza, trae vergüenza a su cabeza.

decisions.choice: having something down from the head: wearing a covering that hangs down over the head
alternatives: having long hair hanging down from the head
decisions.reason: κατὰ κεφαλῆς ἔχων is literally "having down from the head", with the thing itself left unsaid. It is usually taken as a cloth or a fold of the outer garment drawn over the head. Roman men drew the toga over their heads when they led worship or offered sacrifice, and statues show it, so a man praying with his head covered would have been a familiar sight in a Roman colony such as Corinth. Some read it instead of long hair, since verse 14 speaks of a man's long hair as a disgrace. Verse 7 speaks of covering the head with the verb for a covering, which favors a cloth.

decisions.choice: dishonors his head: brings shame both on his own head and on Christ, his head (verse 3)
decisions.reason: Verse 3 has just called Christ the head of every man, and now "head" is used of the man's own head as well. The repeated word lets both senses be heard: what he does with his physical head reflects on Christ. The words alone do not say which is meant first.

decisions.choice: prophesy: speak a message given by God to the gathered church, for its building up, comfort and encouragement
decisions.reason: προφητεύω in Paul is speaking God's word to the church (14:3, 14:24-25, 14:29-31). It may include speaking of the future, but that is not its main sense here. Praying and prophesying together describe taking part aloud in the church's worship.

decisions.choice: with something covering his head
alternatives: having something down from his head
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the Greek means by "having down from the head" (m1). Literal keeps the Greek's unfinished phrase, with the missing word in brackets.

decisions.choice: speaking a message from God
decisions.reason: Readable explains "prophesy" (m3), since many readers think only of predicting the future.

decisions.choice: la tête couverte, se couvrir la tête (verses 4-13)
decisions.reason: "Voile" would name a particular garment, while the Greek speaks only of the head being covered or not, and what the covering was is uncertain (m1 here, m1 at verse 5). French says "se couvrir la tête" and "la tête découverte", as the English says "covering".

decisions.choice: profetiza, comunicando un mensaje de parte de Dios
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the verb "profetizar" and explains it, as Romans 12:6 says "comunicar mensajes de parte de Dios" (m3).

source.text: πᾶσα δὲ γυνὴ προσευχομένη ἢ προφητεύουσα ἀκατακαλύπτῳ τῇ κεφαλῇ καταισχύνει τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτῆς, ἓν γάρ ἐστιν καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ τῇ ἐξυρημένῃ.

records.literal_gloss: Every but woman praying or prophesying uncovered with the head dishonors the head of her, one for it is and the same with the [woman] having been shaved.

en.L: But every woman praying or prophesying with the head uncovered dishonors her head, for it is one and the same [as] the [woman] who has been shaved.
en.B: But a woman who prays or prophesies with nothing over her head shames her head; it is no different from having her head shaved.
en.R: But if a woman prays or prophesies without a covering on her head, she brings shame on her head. It is the same as if she had shaved her head.

fr.L: Mais toute femme qui prie ou prophétise la tête découverte déshonore sa tête, car c’est une seule et même [chose] que la [femme] rasée.
fr.B: Mais une femme qui prie ou prophétise sans rien sur la tête fait honte à sa tête ; cela revient au même que d’avoir la tête rasée.
fr.R: Mais si une femme prie ou prophétise sans avoir la tête couverte, elle fait honte à sa tête. C’est comme si elle s’était rasé la tête.

es.L: Pero toda mujer que ora o profetiza con la cabeza descubierta deshonra su cabeza, porque es una y la misma cosa que [la] que está rapada.
es.B: Pero la mujer que ora o profetiza sin nada que le cubra la cabeza avergüenza a su cabeza; es lo mismo que si se la hubiera rapado.
es.R: Pero si una mujer ora o profetiza sin cubrirse la cabeza, trae vergüenza a su cabeza. Es lo mismo que si se hubiera rapado la cabeza.

decisions.choice: uncovered: without a cloth covering over the head, such as a shawl or the fold of an outer garment
alternatives: with her hair unbound and hanging loose, rather than put up
decisions.reason: ἀκατακαλύπτῳ means "uncovered". Most take it of a covering laid over the head, as was usual for respectable married women in public across the Greek, Roman and Jewish world. Others read it of loose, unbound hair, since a woman's hair let down in public could be a sign of shame or of a loose life, and since verse 15 calls her long hair a covering. Verse 6, which sets "be covered" against having the hair cut off, reads most naturally if the covering is something put over the hair.

decisions.choice: as if she were shaved: a shaved head was a public disgrace for a woman
decisions.reason: A woman's head was shaved as a mark of shame or grief (Deuteronomy 21:12; Isaiah 3:17, 3:24). Paul says that praying uncovered dishonors her as much as that would. ἐξυρημένῃ is a perfect participle: a woman who has been shaved.

decisions.choice: Paul takes for granted that women pray and prophesy aloud when the church meets
decisions.reason: He does not forbid women to pray or prophesy; he speaks of how they should be dressed when they do, as he does for men in verse 4. How this fits 14:34-35, where women are told to be silent, is taken up there.

decisions.choice: no different from having her head shaved (B); as if she had shaved her head (R)
alternatives: one and the same as the shaved woman
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the Greek's "one and the same thing as the shaved woman" into a plain comparison.

source.text: εἰ γὰρ οὐ κατακαλύπτεται γυνή, καὶ κειράσθω· εἰ δὲ αἰσχρὸν γυναικὶ τὸ κείρασθαι ἢ ξυρᾶσθαι, κατακαλυπτέσθω.

records.literal_gloss: If for not is covered a woman, also let her be shorn; if but shameful for a woman the to be shorn or to be shaved, let her be covered.

en.L: For if a woman is not covered, let her also be shorn; but if [it is] shameful for a woman to be shorn or to be shaved, let her be covered.
en.B: If a woman does not wear a covering, let her have her hair cropped too. But if having her hair cropped or shaved off is shameful for a woman, then she should wear a covering.
en.R: If a woman will not cover her head, then let her cut off her hair too. But it is shameful for a woman to cut off her hair or shave her head. So she should cover her head.

fr.L: Car si une femme n’est pas couverte, qu’elle se fasse aussi tondre ; mais si [c’est] une honte pour une femme d’être tondue ou d’être rasée, qu’elle soit couverte.
fr.B: Si une femme ne se couvre pas la tête, qu’elle se fasse aussi couper les cheveux court. Mais s’il est honteux pour une femme d’avoir les cheveux coupés court ou rasés, alors qu’elle se couvre la tête.
fr.R: Si une femme ne veut pas se couvrir la tête, alors qu’elle se coupe aussi les cheveux. Mais c’est une honte pour une femme de se couper les cheveux ou de se raser la tête. Donc elle doit se couvrir la tête.

es.L: Porque si una mujer no se cubre, que también se corte el pelo; pero si [es] vergonzoso para una mujer cortarse el pelo o raparse, que se cubra.
es.B: Si una mujer no se cubre la cabeza, que se corte también el pelo. Pero si es vergonzoso para una mujer cortarse el pelo al rape o raparse, entonces que se cubra.
es.R: Si una mujer no quiere cubrirse la cabeza, que se corte también el pelo. Pero es vergonzoso para una mujer cortarse el pelo o raparse la cabeza. Así que debe cubrirse la cabeza.

decisions.choice: let her also be shorn: not a real command but a way of showing where her choice leads
decisions.reason: κειράσθω is a command in form, but Paul does not want women's hair cut off; the next clause calls that shameful. The "if" clauses build an argument: if she will not cover her head, she may as well go all the way and crop her hair, and since that is shameful, she should be covered.

decisions.choice: shorn ... shaved: to have the hair cut close, or the head shaved bare
decisions.reason: κείρω is to cut or crop the hair short, ξυράομαι to shave it off entirely. Both were marks of disgrace for a woman (verse 5).

decisions.choice: if it is shameful: a condition Paul takes as true
decisions.reason: Paul and his readers agree that a cropped or shaved head shames a woman; the "if" states that agreed fact as the ground of the conclusion.

decisions.choice: But it is shameful ... So she should cover her head.
alternatives: But if it is shameful ..., she should be covered.
decisions.reason: Readable states the condition Paul takes as true as a plain fact (m3) and breaks the sentence into three short ones.

source.text: ἀνὴρ μὲν γὰρ οὐκ ὀφείλει κατακαλύπτεσθαι τὴν κεφαλήν, εἰκὼν καὶ δόξα θεοῦ ὑπάρχων· ἡ γυνὴ δὲ δόξα ἀνδρός ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: A man indeed for not ought to cover the head, image and glory of God being; the woman but glory of man is.

en.L: For a man indeed ought not to cover [his] head, being [the] image and glory of God; but the woman is [the] glory of man.
en.B: A man should not have his head covered, because he is God's image and glory. Woman, for her part, is man's glory.
en.R: A man should not cover his head, because he is made in God's image and shows God's glory. And a woman shows the glory of man.

fr.L: Car l’homme, certes, ne doit pas se couvrir la tête, étant l’image et la gloire de Dieu ; mais la femme est la gloire de l’homme.
fr.B: Un homme ne doit pas avoir la tête couverte, puisqu’il est l’image et la gloire de Dieu. La femme, elle, est la gloire de l’homme.
fr.R: Un homme ne doit pas se couvrir la tête, parce qu’il est créé à l’image de Dieu et qu’il montre la gloire de Dieu. Et la femme montre la gloire de l’homme.

es.L: Porque el hombre ciertamente no debe cubrirse la cabeza, siendo imagen y gloria de Dios; pero la mujer es gloria del hombre.
es.B: El hombre no debe cubrirse la cabeza, porque es imagen y gloria de Dios. La mujer, por su parte, es la gloria del hombre.
es.R: Un hombre no debe cubrirse la cabeza, porque fue creado a la imagen de Dios y muestra la gloria de Dios. Y la mujer muestra la gloria del hombre.

decisions.choice: image ... of God: Genesis 1:26-27, where God makes humankind in his image
decisions.reason: εἰκὼν is the word of the Greek Old Testament in Genesis 1:26-27. Paul does not deny that woman too bears God's image, which Genesis 1:27 says plainly ("male and female he created them"); he goes on to speak of the man's glory, not the woman's lack of the image.

decisions.choice: glory: the one who brings honor to another and makes their worth seen
alternatives: glory: reflected brightness, as of the moon
decisions.reason: δόξα here is honor and reputation: the man brings honor to God, and the woman to the man (as children are the glory of their parents, Proverbs 17:6). The point for worship follows: in the gathered church, the glory that is to be seen is God's, so what reflects on another should be covered. How exactly the woman is man's glory is not spelled out; verses 8-9 explain it from Genesis 2.

decisions.choice: the woman is the glory of man: a statement about the order of creation, not about her worth before God
decisions.reason: Verses 11-12 at once balance this: in the Lord, man and woman are not independent of each other, and man comes into the world through woman. Paul's point is what is fitting when they pray and prophesy, not who is more valued by God.

decisions.choice: is made in God's image and shows God's glory; shows the glory of man
alternatives: is the image and glory of God
decisions.reason: Readable says what it means to be someone's image and glory (m1, m2), keeping the word "glory".

decisions.choice: imagen y gloria, no brackets
decisions.reason: Spanish can leave out the article before "imagen" and "gloria" after "siendo" and "es", as the Greek does, so Literal needs none of the words the English brackets.

source.text: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἀνὴρ ἐκ γυναικός, ἀλλὰ γυνὴ ἐξ ἀνδρός·

records.literal_gloss: Not for is man from woman, but woman from man;

en.L: For man is not from woman, but woman from man;
en.B: Man was not made from woman; woman was made from man.
en.R: In the beginning, God did not make the man from the woman. He made the woman from the man.

fr.L: Car l’homme n’est pas [issu] de la femme, mais la femme de l’homme ;
fr.B: L’homme n’a pas été tiré de la femme ; c’est la femme qui a été tirée de l’homme.
fr.R: Au commencement, Dieu n’a pas fait l’homme à partir de la femme. Il a fait la femme à partir de l’homme.

es.L: Porque el hombre no procede de la mujer, sino la mujer del hombre;
es.B: El hombre no fue hecho de la mujer; la mujer fue hecha del hombre.
es.R: Al principio, Dios no hizo al hombre de la mujer. Hizo a la mujer del hombre.

decisions.choice: woman from man: Genesis 2:21-23, where the woman is made from the man's rib
decisions.reason: Paul is thinking of the first man and woman: "she shall be called woman, because she was taken out of man" (Genesis 2:23). Verse 12 will add the other side, that every man since is born from a woman.

decisions.choice: was made
decisions.reason: The Greek has only "is ... from"; Balanced says that the coming from is the making in Genesis 2 (m1).

decisions.choice: In the beginning, God did not make the man from the woman
decisions.reason: Readable names the creation that Paul refers to (m1), so that the sentence is not read as a claim about how people are born now, which verse 12 states the other way round.

source.text: καὶ γὰρ οὐκ ἐκτίσθη ἀνὴρ διὰ τὴν γυναῖκα, ἀλλὰ γυνὴ διὰ τὸν ἄνδρα.

records.literal_gloss: And for not was created man because of the woman, but woman because of the man.

en.L: For also man was not created because of the woman, but woman because of the man.
en.B: Nor was man created for the sake of woman; woman was created for the sake of man.
en.R: God did not create the man for the woman's sake. He created the woman for the man's sake.

fr.L: Et en effet, l’homme n’a pas été créé à cause de la femme, mais la femme à cause de l’homme.
fr.B: Et l’homme n’a pas été créé pour la femme ; c’est la femme qui a été créée pour l’homme.
fr.R: Dieu n’a pas créé l’homme pour la femme. Il a créé la femme pour l’homme.

es.L: Y tampoco fue creado el hombre por causa de la mujer, sino la mujer por causa del hombre.
es.B: Ni fue creado el hombre para la mujer, sino que la mujer fue creada para el hombre.
es.R: Dios no creó al hombre para el bien de la mujer. Creó a la mujer para el bien del hombre.

decisions.choice: woman created for the sake of man: Genesis 2:18, where God makes the woman as a fitting helper for the man
decisions.reason: ἐκτίσθη ("was created") points to the creation story. In Genesis 2:18 the woman is made because "it is not good for the man to be alone"; the word "helper" there is used of God himself in the Psalms, so it does not mean a lesser being.

decisions.choice: because of: for the sake of
decisions.reason: διὰ with the accusative gives the reason or purpose: the woman was made because the man needed her.

decisions.choice: God did not create; He created
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who created, as the passive implies, and repeats the verb in the second sentence.

source.text: διὰ τοῦτο ὀφείλει ἡ γυνὴ ἐξουσίαν ἔχειν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς διὰ τοὺς ἀγγέλους.

records.literal_gloss: Because of this ought the woman authority to have on the head because of the angels.

en.L: Because of this the woman ought to have authority on [her] head, because of the angels.
en.B: For this reason, and because of the angels, a woman should have authority over her head.
en.R: For this reason a woman should have authority over her own head. The angels are another reason.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi la femme doit avoir une autorité sur la tête, à cause des anges.
fr.B: Pour cette raison, et à cause des anges, la femme doit avoir autorité sur sa tête.
fr.R: Pour cette raison, une femme doit avoir autorité sur sa propre tête. Les anges sont une autre raison.

es.L: Por esto la mujer debe tener autoridad sobre la cabeza, por causa de los ángeles.
es.B: Por esta razón, y por causa de los ángeles, la mujer debe tener autoridad sobre su cabeza.
es.R: Por esta razón la mujer debe tener autoridad sobre su propia cabeza. Los ángeles son otra razón.

decisions.choice: because of this: for the reasons just given in verses 7-9
alternatives: pointing forward to "because of the angels"
decisions.reason: διὰ τοῦτο normally points back. The second "because of" then adds a further reason.

decisions.choice: authority over her head: her own authority, which she is to exercise over her head, the precise sense being uncertain
alternatives: a sign of authority on her head, standing for her husband's authority over her
a sign of authority on her head, standing for her own authority to pray and prophesy
a sign on her head that protects her (with the angels of the next phrase)
decisions.reason: ἐξουσίαν is "authority" or "right", the word Paul used for the Corinthians' rights in 8:9 and his own in chapter 9. Elsewhere in the New Testament, "to have authority" with ἐπὶ and the genitive means to have authority over something (Revelation 11:6; 14:18; 20:6), and nowhere else does the word mean a symbol of someone else's authority. So the Greek most naturally says the woman ought to have authority over her head: she has the right and the duty to decide how it is covered, and should use it as verses 4-9 describe. Older readings took the covering as a sign of being under her husband's authority, and others as the sign of her own authority to take part in worship. This is one of the hardest sentences in Paul, and none of these readings is certain.

decisions.choice: because of the angels: angels who are present when the church worships, and who watch over what is fitting in God's order
alternatives: fallen angels who might be drawn to women, as in one ancient reading of Genesis 6:1-4
human messengers or visitors at the gathering
decisions.reason: Paul says nothing more, so the phrase is open. Angels are elsewhere present to God's people at worship (Psalm 138:1 in the Greek Old Testament, "before angels I will sing your praise"), and Paul says that the apostles are a spectacle to angels (4:9) and that believers will judge angels (6:3). Texts from the Dead Sea Scrolls also speak of angels present in the assembly. The reading that fallen angels lust after women rests on a Jewish interpretation of Genesis 6 and has had defenders, but Paul does not elsewhere speak of angels without qualification as evil. ἀγγέλους is the usual word for angels, not for human messengers.

decisions.choice: on [her] head
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek's own wording, which can be read both as authority over the head and as something on it; Balanced and Readable follow the sense chosen in m2.

decisions.choice: For this reason, and because of the angels, ... (B); The angels are another reason. (R)
alternatives: because of the angels, at the end of the sentence
decisions.reason: Balanced brings both reasons together at the start; Readable gives the angels a short sentence of its own. Neither says why the angels matter, since Paul does not (m3).

decisions.choice: sur la tête
decisions.reason: Like the Greek and the English Literal, French "avoir une autorité sur la tête" can mean both authority over the head and something worn on it; Literal keeps that openness, and needs no bracket, since French uses the article for a part of the body. Balanced and Readable say "sur sa tête", following m2.

decisions.choice: sobre la cabeza, no brackets
decisions.reason: Spanish says "sobre la cabeza" for one's own head with the article alone, so Literal needs no bracketed "[su]".

source.text: πλὴν οὔτε γυνὴ χωρὶς ἀνδρὸς οὔτε ἀνὴρ χωρὶς γυναικὸς ἐν κυρίῳ·

records.literal_gloss: Nevertheless neither woman without man nor man without woman in [the] Lord;

en.L: Nevertheless, neither [is] woman without man nor man without woman in [the] Lord;
en.B: Yet in the Lord there is no woman without man, and no man without woman.
en.R: But among those who belong to the Lord, a woman does not stand apart from a man, and a man does not stand apart from a woman.

fr.L: Toutefois, ni la femme [n’est] sans l’homme, ni l’homme sans la femme, dans le Seigneur ;
fr.B: Pourtant, dans le Seigneur, la femme n’existe pas sans l’homme, ni l’homme sans la femme.
fr.R: Mais parmi ceux qui appartiennent au Seigneur, la femme n’est pas indépendante de l’homme, et l’homme n’est pas indépendant de la femme.

es.L: Sin embargo, ni la mujer [es] sin el hombre, ni el hombre sin la mujer, en [el] Señor;
es.B: Con todo, en el Señor ni la mujer existe sin el hombre, ni el hombre sin la mujer.
es.R: Pero entre los que pertenecen al Señor, la mujer no está separada del hombre, y el hombre no está separado de la mujer.

decisions.choice: nevertheless: a strong turn that limits what verses 7-10 have said
decisions.reason: πλὴν means "only" or "however": Paul guards against reading verses 7-9 as if man had no need of woman.

decisions.choice: neither without the other: man and woman depend on each other and belong together
alternatives: neither is different from the other in the Lord
decisions.reason: χωρὶς is "apart from, without". Neither stands on their own; each owes life and place to the other, as verse 12 explains.

decisions.choice: in the Lord: in the new life of those who belong to Christ
decisions.reason: The order of creation in verses 7-9 is not cancelled, but "in the Lord" it is set within the mutual dependence of men and women (compare Galatians 3:28).

decisions.choice: among those who belong to the Lord
decisions.reason: Readable explains "in the Lord" (m3).

source.text: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡ γυνὴ ἐκ τοῦ ἀνδρός, οὕτως καὶ ὁ ἀνὴρ διὰ τῆς γυναικός· τὰ δὲ πάντα ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Just as for the woman from the man, so also the man through the woman; the but all things from the God.

en.L: For just as the woman [is] from the man, so also the man [is] through the woman; but all things [are] from God.
en.B: Just as woman was made from man, so man is born through woman, and all things have their source in God.
en.R: The first woman was made from the man, but every man since then has been born from a woman. And everything comes from God.

fr.L: Car de même que la femme [vient] de l’homme, de même aussi l’homme [vient] par la femme ; mais tout [vient] de Dieu.
fr.B: De même que la femme a été tirée de l’homme, de même l’homme naît de la femme, et tout a sa source en Dieu.
fr.R: La première femme a été faite à partir de l’homme, mais depuis, chaque homme est né d’une femme. Et tout vient de Dieu.

es.L: Porque así como la mujer [procede] del hombre, así también el hombre [nace] por medio de la mujer; pero todas las cosas [proceden] de Dios.
es.B: Así como la mujer fue hecha del hombre, así también el hombre nace de la mujer, y todo tiene su origen en Dios.
es.R: La primera mujer fue hecha del hombre, pero desde entonces todo hombre ha nacido de una mujer. Y todo viene de Dios.

decisions.choice: the woman from the man ... the man through the woman: the first woman was taken from the man, and every man since is born of a woman
decisions.reason: The first half repeats verse 8 (Genesis 2:21-23); the second turns it round: every man since has come into the world through a mother. The change of preposition, from ἐκ ("from") to διὰ ("through"), marks the difference between the woman's making and every man's birth.

decisions.choice: all things from God: both the order of creation and the birth of every person come from God
decisions.reason: Paul ends by placing man and woman alike under God, the source of all (8:6; Romans 11:36).

decisions.choice: was made ... is born (B); The first woman was made ... every man since then has been born (R)
alternatives: the woman is from the man, the man through the woman
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verbs here. Balanced and Readable supply them to show the two events Paul means (m1); Readable also says "first" and "since then".

source.text: ἐν ὑμῖν αὐτοῖς κρίνατε· πρέπον ἐστὶν γυναῖκα ἀκατακάλυπτον τῷ θεῷ προσεύχεσθαι;

records.literal_gloss: Among you yourselves judge; fitting is it a woman uncovered to the God to pray?

en.L: Judge among yourselves: is it fitting [for] a woman to pray to God uncovered?
en.B: Use your own judgment. When a woman prays to God, is it fitting for her head to be uncovered?
en.R: Think about it for yourselves. Should a woman pray to God without a covering on her head?

fr.L: Jugez entre vous-mêmes : est-il convenable qu’une femme prie Dieu sans être couverte ?
fr.B: Jugez-en vous-mêmes. Quand une femme prie Dieu, convient-il qu’elle ait la tête découverte ?
fr.R: Réfléchissez par vous-mêmes. Une femme doit-elle prier Dieu sans rien sur la tête ?

es.L: {{plural_you:Juzguen|Juzgad}} entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos: ¿es apropiado que una mujer ore a Dios descubierta?
es.B: {{plural_you:Juzguen|Juzgad}} {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos. Cuando una mujer ora a Dios, ¿es apropiado que lleve la cabeza descubierta?
es.R: {{plural_you:Piénsenlo|Pensadlo}} por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos. ¿Debe una mujer orar a Dios sin cubrirse la cabeza?

decisions.choice: fitting: proper, in keeping with what is seemly
decisions.reason: πρέπον appeals to a sense of what suits the occasion, not to a command. Paul expects the Corinthians themselves to agree.

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: Paul asks them to decide for themselves (κρίνατε), confident that they will judge it unfitting.

decisions.choice: When a woman prays to God, is it fitting for her head to be uncovered?
alternatives: is it fitting for a woman to pray to God uncovered?
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the setting first and makes clear that "uncovered" refers to her head.

source.text: οὐδὲ ἡ φύσις αὐτὴ διδάσκει ὑμᾶς ὅτι ἀνὴρ μὲν ἐὰν κομᾷ, ἀτιμία αὐτῷ ἐστιν, γυνὴ δὲ ἐὰν κομᾷ, δόξα αὐτῇ ἐστιν;

records.literal_gloss: Not even the nature itself teaches you that a man indeed if he has long hair, a dishonor to him it is, \v 15 a woman but if she has long hair, glory to her it is?

en.L: Does not even nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a dishonor to him, \v 15 but if a woman has long hair, it is a glory to her?
en.B: Is it not nature itself that teaches you this: for a man, long hair is a dishonor, \v 15 but for a woman, long hair is her glory?
en.R: Even the way things naturally are shows you that long hair is a shame for a man. \v 15 But for a woman, long hair is her glory.

fr.L: La nature elle-même ne vous enseigne-t-elle pas que si un homme porte les cheveux longs, c’est un déshonneur pour lui, \v 15 mais que si une femme porte les cheveux longs, c’est une gloire pour elle ?
fr.B: N’est-ce pas la nature elle-même qui vous l’enseigne : pour un homme, les cheveux longs sont un déshonneur, \v 15 mais pour une femme, les cheveux longs sont sa gloire ?
fr.R: Même l’ordre naturel des choses vous le montre : les cheveux longs sont une honte pour un homme. \v 15 Mais pour une femme, les cheveux longs sont sa gloire.

es.L: ¿No {{plural_you:les|os}} enseña la naturaleza misma que si el hombre se deja crecer el pelo, le es deshonra, \v 15 pero si la mujer se deja crecer el pelo, le es gloria?
es.B: ¿No es la naturaleza misma la que {{plural_you:les|os}} enseña esto: que para el hombre es una deshonra llevar el pelo largo, \v 15 pero que para la mujer el pelo largo es su gloria?
es.R: Hasta el orden natural de las cosas {{plural_you:les|os}} muestra que el pelo largo es una vergüenza para el hombre. \v 15 Pero para la mujer, el pelo largo es su gloria.

decisions.choice: nature: the way things are, as people of that time felt them to be, including the settled customs that seemed natural to them
alternatives: the created order, apart from any custom
decisions.reason: φύσις in Paul can mean the created order (Romans 1:26-27) or the way things simply are (Romans 2:14; Galatians 2:15). Men's hair length was in fact a matter of custom, and the Nazirite vow had men grow their hair long (Numbers 6:5). So Paul appeals to a feeling for what is natural, shared by his readers, that a man's long hair and a woman's short hair look wrong.

decisions.choice: have long hair: let the hair grow long
decisions.reason: κομάω means to wear the hair long. In that world men usually wore their hair short and women long.

decisions.choice: glory: honor, something that becomes her
decisions.reason: δόξα is set against ἀτιμία ("dishonor"), so here it means honor or adornment, as in verse 7.

decisions.choice: Even the way things naturally are shows you ... But for a woman, long hair is her glory.
alternatives: Does not nature itself teach you ...?
decisions.reason: Paul's question expects the answer yes; Readable turns it into a statement so the point is not missed.

decisions.choice: the way things naturally are
decisions.reason: Readable explains "nature" in plain words (m1).

decisions.choice: gloria
decisions.reason: The word here means honor, something that becomes her (m3). Spanish keeps "gloria", the key term, at every level, as the English keeps "glory", so it answers verse 7.

source.text: ὅτι ἡ κόμη ἀντὶ περιβολαίου δέδοται.

records.literal_gloss: Because the long hair instead of a covering has been given.

en.L: For the long hair has been given [to her] for a covering.
en.B: Long hair was given to her to serve as a covering.
en.R: God has given her long hair as a covering.

fr.L: Car la chevelure [lui] a été donnée en guise de couverture.
fr.B: Les cheveux longs lui ont été donnés pour la couvrir.
fr.R: Dieu lui a donné les cheveux longs pour la couvrir.

es.L: Porque el pelo largo [le] ha sido dado en lugar de velo.
es.B: El pelo largo se le dio para que le sirva de velo.
es.R: Dios le ha dado a la mujer el pelo largo como velo.

decisions.choice: for a covering: as a covering, matching the covering she wears
alternatives: instead of a covering, so that no other covering is needed
decisions.reason: ἀντὶ usually means "instead of", but it can also mean "for, as" (compare "grace for grace", John 1:16). If it meant that her hair replaces a covering, the argument of verses 5-6 and 13 would fall apart; Paul's point is that nature has already given her a covering, and so shows that a covering suits her.

decisions.choice: covering: a wrap or mantle thrown around the body or head
decisions.reason: περιβόλαιον is a wrap or cloak, a different word from the verb "cover" in verses 5-7.

decisions.choice: has been given: given by God, in the way things are made
decisions.reason: δέδοται is a passive whose giver is God, the one from whom are all things (verse 12).

decisions.choice: God has given
decisions.reason: Readable names the giver (m3).

decisions.choice: velo
decisions.reason: The word is a wrap or mantle around the head or body (m2). Spanish "velo" is the plain word for a woman's head covering; "manto" is kept for the outer garment in the Gospels.

source.text: εἰ δέ τις δοκεῖ φιλόνεικος εἶναι, ἡμεῖς τοιαύτην συνήθειαν οὐκ ἔχομεν, οὐδὲ αἱ ἐκκλησίαι τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: If but anyone seems contentious to be, we such a custom not have, nor the churches of the God.

en.L: But if anyone seems to be contentious, we do not have such a custom, nor [do] the churches of God.
en.B: If anyone wants to dispute it, we recognize no such custom, and neither do the churches of God.
en.R: Someone may want to argue about this. But we have no custom of women praying with uncovered heads, and neither do any of God's churches.

fr.L: Mais si quelqu’un paraît aimer la querelle, nous n’avons pas une telle coutume, ni les églises de Dieu.
fr.B: Si quelqu’un veut contester ce point, nous ne connaissons pas une telle coutume, et les églises de Dieu non plus.
fr.R: Quelqu’un voudra peut-être discuter de cela. Mais ni nous ni aucune des églises de Dieu n’avons pour coutume que les femmes prient la tête découverte.

es.L: Pero si alguno parece ser contencioso, nosotros no tenemos tal costumbre, ni las iglesias de Dios.
es.B: Si alguien quiere discutirlo, nosotros no reconocemos tal costumbre, y tampoco las iglesias de Dios.
es.R: Puede que alguien quiera discutir sobre esto. Pero nosotros no tenemos la costumbre de que las mujeres oren con la cabeza descubierta, y tampoco la tiene ninguna de las iglesias de Dios.

decisions.choice: custom: an established practice in the churches
decisions.reason: συνήθεια is what people are used to doing, a settled practice. Paul ends the argument by appealing to what all the churches do (as in 4:17; 7:17; 14:33).

decisions.choice: such a custom: the practice of women praying and prophesying with uncovered heads
alternatives: any custom of head coverings at all
decisions.reason: τοιαύτην ("such") points back to what Paul has argued against. Some take it as the habit of arguing, which the sentence has just mentioned, but the appeal to "the churches of God" fits a practice in worship best. The reading that Paul means no churches require head coverings would contradict everything he has just said.

decisions.choice: seems to be contentious: is inclined to go on arguing, is set on a quarrel
decisions.reason: φιλόνεικος is someone who loves strife. δοκεῖ ("thinks, seems") here has the sense of being inclined.

decisions.choice: no custom of women praying with uncovered heads
decisions.reason: Readable says which custom is meant (m2). Since that is not certain, this expansion is marked for reviewers.

decisions.choice: Someone may want to argue about this. But ...
decisions.reason: Readable splits the condition into its own sentence.

decisions.choice: les églises de Dieu, lowercase (for chapters 11-13)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the different congregations, so it takes a small letter, as the style guide sets for one local church; "l’Église" with a capital is kept for the church of God as a whole (verse 22; 12:28).

source.text: Τοῦτο δὲ παραγγέλλων οὐκ ἐπαινῶ ὅτι οὐκ εἰς τὸ κρεῖσσον ἀλλὰ εἰς τὸ ἧσσον συνέρχεσθε.

records.literal_gloss: This but instructing not I praise, because not for the better but for the worse you come together.

en.L: But in giving this instruction I do not praise [you], because you come together not for the better but for the worse.
en.B: But as I give you this next instruction, I do not praise you, because when you come together, it makes things worse, not better.
en.R: But in what I must tell you now, I cannot praise you. Your meetings make things worse instead of better.

fr.L: Mais en vous donnant cette instruction, je ne [vous] loue pas, parce que vous vous réunissez non pour le meilleur, mais pour le pire.
fr.B: Mais en vous donnant la consigne qui suit, je ne vous félicite pas, car vos réunions vous font du tort au lieu de vous faire du bien.
fr.R: Mais dans ce que je dois vous dire maintenant, je ne peux pas vous féliciter. Vos réunions font plus de mal que de bien.

es.L: Pero al dar esta instrucción no [{{plural_you:los|os}}] alabo, porque no {{plural_you:se reúnen|os reunís}} para lo mejor sino para lo peor.
es.B: Pero al {{plural_you:darles|daros}} esta otra instrucción, no {{plural_you:los|os}} alabo, porque cuando {{plural_you:se reúnen|os reunís}}, las cosas empeoran en lugar de mejorar.
es.R: Pero en lo que ahora tengo que {{plural_you:decirles|deciros}}, no {{plural_you:los|os}} puedo alabar. {{plural_you:Sus|Vuestras}} reuniones hacen que las cosas vayan peor en lugar de mejor.

decisions.choice: this instruction: what follows in verses 17-34
alternatives: the instructions on head coverings just given
decisions.reason: Τοῦτο can point back or forward. Here "I do not praise" answers "I praise you" of verse 2, and the reason given ("because you come together ... for the worse") belongs to the new subject of the meal, so it most likely points forward.

decisions.choice: come together: meet as the church, for worship and the shared meal
decisions.reason: συνέρχομαι runs through this section (verses 18, 20, 33, 34; and 14:23, 14:26) for the gathering of the church.

decisions.choice: when you come together, it makes things worse, not better (B); your meetings make things worse instead of better (R)
alternatives: you come together not for the better but for the worse
decisions.reason: The Greek "for the better ... for the worse" is turned round into plain speech; Literal keeps it.

source.text: πρῶτον μὲν γὰρ συνερχομένων ὑμῶν ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ ἀκούω σχίσματα ἐν ὑμῖν ὑπάρχειν, καὶ μέρος τι πιστεύω.

records.literal_gloss: First indeed for coming together of you in church I hear divisions among you to exist, and part some I believe.

en.L: For first, when you come together in church, I hear that divisions exist among you, and in part I believe [it].
en.B: To begin with, I am told that when you gather as a church you are split into groups, and I believe some of it.
en.R: First, people tell me that when you meet together as a church, you split into groups. And I believe that some of this is true.

fr.L: Car d’abord, quand vous vous réunissez en église, j’entends dire qu’il existe des divisions parmi vous, et je [le] crois en partie.
fr.B: Tout d’abord, on me dit que, lorsque vous vous réunissez en église, vous êtes divisés en groupes, et je le crois en partie.
fr.R: D’abord, on me dit que, quand vous vous réunissez comme église, vous vous séparez en groupes. Et je crois qu’il y a du vrai là-dedans.

es.L: Porque, en primer lugar, cuando {{plural_you:se reúnen|os reunís}} en asamblea, oigo que hay divisiones entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y en parte [lo] creo.
es.B: Para empezar, me dicen que cuando {{plural_you:se reúnen|os reunís}} como iglesia, {{plural_you:se dividen|os dividís}} en grupos, y en parte lo creo.
es.R: Primero, me cuentan que cuando {{plural_you:se reúnen|os reunís}} como iglesia, {{plural_you:se dividen|os dividís}} en grupos. Y creo que algo de eso es verdad.

decisions.choice: in church: as an assembly, when the believers meet
decisions.reason: ἐκκλησίᾳ without the article means "in assembly". The church met in homes; there were no church buildings.

decisions.choice: divisions: splits within the gathering, here between those who have plenty and those who have little
decisions.reason: σχίσμα is the word of 1:10, but verses 21-22 show what these divisions are: some eat and drink their fill while others go hungry. They follow the lines of wealth and standing more than loyalty to a teacher.

decisions.choice: first: the first of the matters about their gatherings
decisions.reason: πρῶτον μὲν leads us to expect a "second", which never comes in so many words. Chapters 12-14, on gifts in the gathering, may be the next matter.

decisions.choice: you are split into groups (B); you split into groups (R)
decisions.reason: As at 1:10, Balanced and Readable describe the splitting rather than using the abstract noun; Literal keeps "divisions".

decisions.choice: en asamblea
decisions.reason: The word here means the gathering of believers (m1), not a building, so Literal says "en asamblea" rather than "en la iglesia"; Balanced and Readable say "como iglesia".

decisions.choice: divisiones
decisions.reason: The same word as in 1:10, where Spanish says "divisiones"; "facciones" is kept for the different word of verse 19.

source.text: δεῖ γὰρ καὶ αἱρέσεις ἐν ὑμῖν εἶναι, ἵνα καὶ οἱ δόκιμοι φανεροὶ γένωνται ἐν ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: It is necessary for also factions among you to be, so that also the approved evident may become among you.

en.L: For there must also be factions among you, so that the approved also may become evident among you.
en.B: For factions among you are bound to come, so that those who stand the test may be seen for what they are.
en.R: Groups like these are bound to come, and they make it clear which of you are genuine.

fr.L: Car il faut aussi qu’il y ait des factions parmi vous, afin que ceux qui sont approuvés deviennent aussi manifestes parmi vous.
fr.B: Il faut bien qu’il y ait des factions parmi vous, pour que ceux qui résistent à l’épreuve soient reconnus pour ce qu’ils sont.
fr.R: Ces groupes doivent forcément apparaître, et ils montrent clairement lesquels d’entre vous sont authentiques.

es.L: Porque también es necesario que haya facciones entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, para que también los aprobados se hagan evidentes entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Porque es inevitable que surjan facciones entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, para que se vea quiénes pasan la prueba.
es.R: Es inevitable que haya grupos así, y eso deja claro quiénes de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} son auténticos.

decisions.choice: factions: groups that take sides against each other
decisions.reason: αἵρεσις is a party or faction (Acts 5:17; 15:5); the later sense of "heresy" came after the New Testament. Here it is another word for the divisions of verse 18.

decisions.choice: there must be factions: God allows even these divisions and uses them to show who is genuine
alternatives: Paul speaks with bitter irony about those who think themselves the approved ones
a plain statement that such divisions must come before the end (as Jesus warned, Matthew 24:10-12)
decisions.reason: δεῖ often speaks of what must happen in God's purpose. Paul does not approve the factions; he says that they bring to light who is δόκιμοι, tested and proved true. Many hear irony too: the ones who set themselves apart think they are the approved, but the test of the meal shows otherwise.

decisions.choice: those who stand the test
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of δόκιμοι, those tested and found genuine.

decisions.choice: los aprobados (L); quiénes pasan la prueba (B)
decisions.reason: The word is the one for being tested and found genuine. Literal says "aprobados", the word kept for this family in the Corinthian letters; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

source.text: συνερχομένων οὖν ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ οὐκ ἔστιν κυριακὸν δεῖπνον φαγεῖν, ἕκαστος γὰρ τὸ ἴδιον δεῖπνον προλαμβάνει ἐν τῷ φαγεῖν, καὶ ὃς μὲν πεινᾷ, ὃς δὲ μεθύει.

records.literal_gloss: Coming together then of you at the same [place] not it is [the] Lord's supper to eat, \v 21 each one for the own supper takes beforehand in the eating, and one is hungry, another is drunk.

en.L: So when you come together in the same [place], it is not [the] Lord's supper [that you] eat, \v 21 for in the eating each one goes ahead with his own supper, and one is hungry and another is drunk.
en.B: So when you gather in one place, what you eat is not really the Lord's Supper. \v 21 Each of you, as you eat, goes ahead with your own meal; one is left hungry, and another is drunk.
en.R: When you meet together, you are not really eating the Lord's Supper. \v 21 Each of you eats your own food without waiting for the others. Some go hungry, while others drink so much that they get drunk.

fr.L: Quand donc vous vous réunissez au même [endroit], ce n’est pas le repas du Seigneur [que vous] mangez, \v 21 car en mangeant chacun prend d’avance son propre repas, et l’un a faim, l’autre est ivre.
fr.B: Ainsi, quand vous vous réunissez en un même lieu, ce n’est pas vraiment le repas du Seigneur que vous prenez. \v 21 Car au moment de manger, chacun se hâte de prendre son propre repas ; l’un reste sur sa faim, et l’autre est ivre.
fr.R: Quand vous vous réunissez, vous ne prenez pas vraiment le repas du Seigneur. \v 21 Chacun mange sa propre nourriture sans attendre les autres. Certains ont faim, tandis que d’autres boivent tellement qu’ils sont ivres.

es.L: Así pues, cuando {{plural_you:se reúnen|os reunís}} en un mismo [lugar], no es [la] cena del Señor [lo que] {{plural_you:comen|coméis}}, \v 21 porque al comer cada uno se adelanta a tomar su propia cena, y uno pasa hambre y otro se emborracha.
es.B: Así que, cuando {{plural_you:se reúnen|os reunís}} en un mismo lugar, lo que {{plural_you:comen|coméis}} no es realmente la Cena del Señor. \v 21 Al comer, cada uno se adelanta a tomar su propia comida, y uno se queda con hambre mientras otro se emborracha.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:se reúnen|os reunís}}, no {{plural_you:están|estáis}} comiendo realmente la Cena del Señor. \v 21 Cada uno come su propia comida sin esperar a los demás. Algunos se quedan con hambre, mientras otros beben tanto que se emborrachan.

decisions.choice: the Lord's supper: the meal belonging to the Lord, a full shared meal at which the bread and the cup were taken
decisions.reason: δεῖπνον is the main evening meal. In the early church the believers ate together in a home, and the bread and cup of verses 23-25 belonged within the meal ("after supper", verse 25). κυριακὸν means "belonging to the Lord"; the meal is his, not theirs to use as they please.

decisions.choice: it is not the Lord's supper that you eat: what they do no longer deserves that name
alternatives: it is not possible to eat the Lord's supper in this way
decisions.reason: With an infinitive, "it is not" can mean "it is not possible". Either way the point is the same: their selfish meal has stopped being the Lord's.

decisions.choice: goes ahead with: eats one's own meal before others arrive, or without sharing it
decisions.reason: προλαμβάνει normally means to take or do something beforehand. Verse 33, "wait for one another", fits that sense: those with leisure and food began without the poorer believers, who may have come later after work. In some writings of the time the word means simply "eat", and then Paul's point is that each eats their own food without sharing.

decisions.choice: one is hungry, another is drunk: the poor go without while the well-off eat and drink their fill
decisions.reason: In a Roman house the host's friends of equal rank dined in the dining room with better food, while others were placed elsewhere with less. Brought into the church, such customs shamed those who had nothing (verse 22).

decisions.choice: the Lord's Supper
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the name by which the meal is still known; Literal writes "[the] Lord's supper" in lower case, as a description of a meal that belongs to the Lord (m1).

decisions.choice: without waiting for the others
decisions.reason: Readable says what "going ahead" means in this setting (m3, verse 33).

decisions.choice: le repas du Seigneur
decisions.reason: "La Cène" is the church name, but it hides that Paul is speaking of a real shared meal (m1), and it is unfamiliar to new readers. "Le repas du Seigneur" is both a description and a name still used in French churches, so it serves every level; French has no capital to mark the difference the English makes between Literal and the other levels.

decisions.choice: cena del Señor (L); la Cena del Señor (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable write "la Cena del Señor" with a capital, as the name of the meal (as Acts 20:7 does in Spanish); Literal keeps the plain words of the Greek (m1).

source.text: μὴ γὰρ οἰκίας οὐκ ἔχετε εἰς τὸ ἐσθίειν καὶ πίνειν;

records.literal_gloss: Not for houses not you have for the to eat and to drink?

en.L: For do you not have houses for eating and drinking?
en.B: Surely you have homes of your own for eating and drinking?
en.R: Do you not have homes where you can eat and drink?

fr.L: Car n’avez-vous pas de maisons pour manger et boire ?
fr.B: N’avez-vous pas, tout de même, vos maisons pour manger et boire ?
fr.R: Vous n’avez pas de maison pour manger et boire ?

es.L: ¿Pues no {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} casas para comer y beber?
es.B: ¿Acaso no {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} casas propias para comer y beber?
es.R: ¿No {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} casas donde comer y beber?

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer yes: of course you have homes
decisions.reason: μὴ with οὐκ makes a question that expects agreement. Paul is not against eating; he is against using the church's meal as a private dinner party (verse 34).

decisions.choice: Surely you have homes of your own
decisions.reason: Balanced shows that the question expects the answer yes.

source.text: ἢ τῆς ἐκκλησίας τοῦ θεοῦ καταφρονεῖτε, καὶ καταισχύνετε τοὺς μὴ ἔχοντας;

records.literal_gloss: Or the church of the God do you despise, and put to shame those not having?

en.L: Or do you despise the church of God and put to shame those who do not have?
en.B: Or do you look down on God's church and shame those who have nothing?
en.R: Or do you treat God's church with contempt and make poor believers feel ashamed?

fr.L: Ou bien méprisez-vous l’Église de Dieu et faites-vous honte à ceux qui n’ont [rien] ?
fr.B: Ou méprisez-vous l’Église de Dieu, et humiliez-vous ceux qui n’ont rien ?
fr.R: Ou bien traitez-vous l’Église de Dieu avec mépris, et faites-vous honte aux croyants pauvres ?

es.L: ¿O {{plural_you:desprecian|despreciáis}} la iglesia de Dios y {{plural_you:avergüenzan|avergonzáis}} a los que no tienen?
es.B: ¿O es que {{plural_you:menosprecian|menospreciáis}} la iglesia de Dios y {{plural_you:humillan|humilláis}} a los que no tienen nada?
es.R: ¿O es que {{plural_you:tratan|tratáis}} con desprecio a la iglesia de Dios y {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} que los creyentes pobres se sientan avergonzados?

decisions.choice: the church of God: God's people gathered, not a building
decisions.reason: To despise the poorer members at the meal is to despise the church that belongs to God (1:2; 10:32).

decisions.choice: those who do not have: the poor, who have little or nothing to bring
decisions.reason: τοὺς μὴ ἔχοντας has no object. After "houses" it could mean those with no homes of their own, but it most naturally means the poor in general, who have nothing (as in 2 Corinthians 8:12).

decisions.choice: poor believers
decisions.reason: Readable names the people meant (m2).

decisions.choice: l’Église de Dieu, with a capital
decisions.reason: The Corinthians are gathered as one congregation, but "the church of God" names it as God's own people (m1), the church as such that each gathering makes present, so French uses the capital, as for the church as a whole; "les églises de Dieu" in verse 16 are the congregations and stay lowercase.

source.text: τί εἴπω ὑμῖν;

records.literal_gloss: What should I say to you?

en.L: What should I say to you?
en.B: What am I to say to you?
en.R: What can I say to you?

fr.L: Que vous dirai-je ?
fr.B: Que dois-je vous dire ?
fr.R: Que puis-je vous dire ?

es.L: ¿Qué {{plural_you:les|os}} diré?
es.B: ¿Qué voy a {{plural_you:decirles|deciros}}?
es.R: ¿Qué puedo {{plural_you:decirles|deciros}}?

decisions.choice: what should I say: a deliberative question, expressing dismay
decisions.reason: εἴπω is a subjunctive of deliberation: Paul is at a loss for words.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:decirles|deciros}}
decisions.reason: Where the plural "you" is joined to the end of a verb, the two Spanish forms differ in the ending, so the span covers the whole verb, as in 2:1.

source.text: ἐπαινέσω ὑμᾶς;

records.literal_gloss: Shall I praise you?

en.L: Shall I praise you?
en.B: Should I praise you?
en.R: Should I praise you for this?

fr.L: Vous louerai-je ?
fr.B: Faut-il vous féliciter ?
fr.R: Est-ce que je dois vous féliciter pour cela ?

es.L: ¿{{plural_you:Los|Os}} alabaré?
es.B: ¿Debo {{plural_you:alabarlos|alabaros}}?
es.R: ¿Debo {{plural_you:alabarlos|alabaros}} por esto?

decisions.choice: shall I praise you: a question expecting no, which looks back to "I praise you" in verse 2
decisions.reason: ἐπαινέσω takes up the verb of 11:2 and 11:17; the answer follows at once.

decisions.choice: for this
decisions.reason: Readable adds what the praise would be for, which the next sentence states.

source.text: ἐν τούτῳ οὐκ ἐπαινῶ.

records.literal_gloss: In this not I praise.

en.L: In this I do not praise [you].
en.B: In this matter, no, I do not praise you.
en.R: No, I will not praise you for this.

fr.L: En cela je ne [vous] loue pas.
fr.B: Sur ce point, non, je ne vous félicite pas.
fr.R: Non, je ne vais pas vous féliciter pour cela.

es.L: En esto no [{{plural_you:los|os}}] alabo.
es.B: En esto, no, no {{plural_you:los|os}} alabo.
es.R: No, no {{plural_you:los|os}} alabaré por esto.

decisions.choice: follow the SBLGNT: "Shall I praise you? In this I do not praise you."
alternatives: "Shall I praise you in this? I do not praise you."
decisions.reason: Ancient manuscripts have little punctuation. ἐν τούτῳ ("in this") can be read with the question before or with the answer after; the meaning is the same either way.

source.text: Ἐγὼ γὰρ παρέλαβον ἀπὸ τοῦ κυρίου, ὃ καὶ παρέδωκα ὑμῖν, ὅτι ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῇ νυκτὶ ᾗ παρεδίδετο ἔλαβεν ἄρτον καὶ εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ εἶπεν· Τοῦτό μού ἐστιν τὸ σῶμα τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν· τοῦτο ποιεῖτε εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν.

records.literal_gloss: I for received from the Lord, what also I handed on to you, that the Lord Jesus in the night in which he was being handed over took bread \v 24 and having given thanks broke and said, This of me is the body that for you; this do for the my remembrance.

en.L: For I received from the Lord what I also handed on to you, that the Lord Jesus, in the night in which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was being handed over, took bread \v 24 and, having given thanks, broke [it] and said, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body, which [is] for you; do this for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} remembrance."
en.B: What I handed on to you, I myself received from the Lord: on the night {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was handed over, the Lord Jesus took bread, \v 24 gave thanks and broke it, saying, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body; it is for you. Do this to remember {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: I received this from the Lord, and I passed it on to you. On the night {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was handed over to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies, the Lord Jesus took some bread. \v 24 He thanked God for it, broke it, and said, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body. It is for you. Do this to remember {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

fr.L: Car moi, j’ai reçu du Seigneur ce que je vous ai aussi transmis, [à savoir] que le Seigneur Jésus, dans la nuit où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était livré, prit du pain \v 24 et, ayant rendu grâce, [le] rompit et dit : « Ceci est {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} corps, qui [est] pour vous ; faites ceci en {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} mémoire. »
fr.B: Ce que je vous ai transmis, je l’ai moi-même reçu du Seigneur : la nuit où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fut livré, le Seigneur Jésus prit du pain, \v 24 rendit grâce, le rompit et dit : « Ceci est {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} corps ; il est pour vous. Faites cela pour vous souvenir de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. »
fr.R: J’ai reçu cela du Seigneur, et je vous l’ai transmis. La nuit où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a été livré à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} ennemis, le Seigneur Jésus a pris du pain. \v 24 Il a remercié Dieu pour ce pain, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’a rompu et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a dit : « Ceci est {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} corps. Il est pour vous. Faites cela pour vous souvenir de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. »

es.L: Porque yo recibí del Señor lo que también {{plural_you:les|os}} transmití: que el Señor Jesús, en la noche en que era entregado, tomó pan, \v 24 y habiendo dado gracias, [lo] partió y dijo: «Esto es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cuerpo, que [es] por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} esto en recuerdo {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}».
es.B: Lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} transmití, yo mismo lo recibí del Señor: la noche en que fue entregado, el Señor Jesús tomó pan, \v 24 dio gracias, lo partió y dijo: «Esto es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cuerpo; es por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} esto en recuerdo de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}».
es.R: Yo recibí esto del Señor, y {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} transmití a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. La noche en que fue entregado a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} enemigos, el Señor Jesús tomó un pan. \v 24 Dio gracias a Dios por él, lo partió y dijo: «Esto es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cuerpo. Es por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} esto {{plural_you:para acordarse|para acordaros}} de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}».

decisions.choice: received ... handed on: the words used for passing on a tradition faithfully, as one generation of teachers to the next
decisions.reason: παρέλαβον and παρέδωκα are the same pair Paul uses for the gospel in 15:3, and for the traditions in 11:2. They mark what follows as teaching he was given and passed on unchanged.

decisions.choice: from the Lord: the tradition goes back to the Lord Jesus himself, though it reached Paul through those who were believers before him
alternatives: a direct revelation from the risen Lord to Paul
decisions.reason: ἀπὸ ("from") names where the tradition began, not necessarily how it reached him. The account matches the one in Luke 22:19-20 closely, which suggests a tradition shared by the churches; yet Paul also says that he received his gospel by revelation (Galatians 1:12). Here the language of passing on points to the shared tradition, with the Lord as its source.

decisions.choice: was handed over: handed over to his enemies, by Judas and, behind that, in God's purpose
decisions.reason: παρεδίδετο is the same verb as "handed on" in this sentence. It is used of Judas handing Jesus over (Mark 14:10), and of God giving up his Son (Romans 4:25; 8:32). The imperfect tense pictures it as under way that very night. "Betrayed" names only Judas's part.

decisions.choice: follow the SBLGNT: "which is for you", with no verb
alternatives: "which is given for you" (as in Luke 22:19)
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts have only "which is for you". Many later manuscripts add "broken", and some "given", to fill out the short phrase. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: for my remembrance: so as to call me to mind, to remember what I have done
decisions.reason: ἀνάμνησιν is remembering that makes the past present and acts on it. Israel kept the Passover "as a memorial" of its rescue from Egypt (Exodus 12:14), and this meal took place at Passover time. To remember Jesus at the meal is to call to mind his death "for you" and to proclaim it (verse 26).

decisions.choice: having given thanks: having said the blessing over the bread
decisions.reason: εὐχαριστήσας refers to the Jewish thanksgiving to God said over bread at a meal; the later name for the Lord's Supper, the Eucharist, comes from this word.

decisions.choice: What I handed on to you, I myself received from the Lord
alternatives: For I received from the Lord what I also handed on to you
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the teaching they already have first and stresses Paul's Ἐγὼ ("I") with "I myself".

decisions.choice: to remember {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plain verb; Literal keeps the noun ("for my remembrance").

decisions.choice: handed over to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies; thanked God for it
alternatives: was handed over; having given thanks
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom he was handed over and to whom the thanks were given (m3, m6).

decisions.choice: "j’ai reçu", "je vous ai transmis" at every level; the account of the supper in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("prit", "rompit", "dit"), in the passé composé at Readable ("a pris", "a dit")
alternatives: passé composé for the whole sentence at every level
decisions.reason: Paul speaks to his readers about what he received and handed on, so those verbs are in the passé composé, as everywhere in the letter. What he hands on is a short narrative of the Lord's last night, and French tells such an account in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced and in the passé composé at Readable, as the style guide sets for narration inside a letter; verse 25 continues in the same tenses.

decisions.choice: en {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} mémoire (L); pour vous souvenir de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek possessive with the noun ("my remembrance"); Balanced and Readable use the verb, as the English does.

decisions.choice: en recuerdo {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}} (L); en recuerdo de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} (B); {{plural_you:para acordarse|para acordaros}} de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} (R)
decisions.reason: The same Spanish words as Luke 22:19, where the Greek is the same, so the two accounts of the Supper read alike.

decisions.choice: era entregado (L); fue entregado (B, R), no pronoun
decisions.reason: Spanish leaves the subject in the verb, so there is no pronoun for the English deity_pronoun span. "Entregar" keeps the Greek verb, which is also "handed on" in this verse (m1, m3); "traicionar" would name only Judas.

source.text: ὡσαύτως καὶ τὸ ποτήριον μετὰ τὸ δειπνῆσαι, λέγων· Τοῦτο τὸ ποτήριον ἡ καινὴ διαθήκη ἐστὶν ἐν τῷ ἐμῷ αἵματι· τοῦτο ποιεῖτε, ὁσάκις ἐὰν πίνητε, εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν.

records.literal_gloss: Likewise also the cup after the to dine, saying, This the cup the new covenant is in the my blood; this do, as often as you drink, for the my remembrance.

en.L: Likewise also the cup, after the supping, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood; do this, as often as you drink [it], for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} remembrance."
en.B: He did the same with the cup once supper was over, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood. Every time you drink it, do this to remember {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: When the meal was over, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the cup in the same way and said, "This cup is God's new covenant, made through {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood. Every time you drink from it, do this to remember {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

fr.L: De même aussi la coupe, après avoir soupé, disant : « Cette coupe est la nouvelle alliance en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} sang ; faites ceci, toutes les fois que vous [en] boirez, en {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} mémoire. »
fr.B: Il fit de même avec la coupe, une fois le repas terminé, en disant : « Cette coupe est la nouvelle alliance en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} sang. Chaque fois que vous en boirez, faites cela pour vous souvenir de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. »
fr.R: À la fin du repas, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a pris la coupe de la même façon et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a dit : « Cette coupe est la nouvelle alliance de Dieu, conclue par {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} sang. Chaque fois que vous en buvez, faites cela pour vous souvenir de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. »

es.L: Asimismo también la copa, después de haber cenado, diciendo: «Esta copa es el nuevo pacto en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} sangre; {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} esto, cada vez que [la] {{plural_you:beban|bebáis}}, en recuerdo {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}».
es.B: Del mismo modo, después de la cena tomó la copa y dijo: «Esta copa es el nuevo pacto en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} sangre. Cada vez que la {{plural_you:beban|bebáis}}, {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} esto en recuerdo de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}».
es.R: Cuando terminó la cena, tomó la copa de la misma manera y dijo: «Esta copa es el nuevo pacto de Dios, hecho con {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} sangre. Cada vez que {{plural_you:beban|bebáis}} de ella, {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} esto {{plural_you:para acordarse|para acordaros}} de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}».

decisions.choice: the new covenant in my blood: Jeremiah 31:31-34 and Exodus 24:8
decisions.reason: God promised through Jeremiah a καινὴ διαθήκη, "new covenant", in which he would forgive his people's sins and write his law on their hearts. At Sinai the covenant was sealed with the blood of sacrifices, "the blood of the covenant" (Exodus 24:8). Jesus says that the new covenant is made by his own blood, that is, by his death.

decisions.choice: in my blood: by means of my blood, which makes the covenant
decisions.reason: ἐν here gives the means: the covenant is established through the blood of Jesus. The cup is called the covenant because it is the sign by which they share in it.

decisions.choice: after supper: the cup was taken when the meal was over, as one of the cups of a Jewish festive meal
decisions.reason: The bread came at the start of the meal and the cup at the end. At the Passover meal, a cup of blessing followed the main course (compare "the cup of blessing", 10:16).

decisions.choice: He did the same with the cup (B); {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the cup in the same way (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the verb to be understood from verses 23-24; Balanced and Readable supply it.

decisions.choice: God's new covenant, made through {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the maker of the covenant (Jeremiah 31:31) and says what "in my blood" means (m2).

decisions.choice: la nouvelle alliance
decisions.reason: "Alliance" is the style guide's word for covenant in every book; it keeps the link with Jeremiah 31:31 (m1), where God promises a new covenant. "Testament" would now be read as a will or as the name of the second part of the Bible.

decisions.choice: pacto
decisions.reason: As in Luke 22:20: the new covenant God promised through Jeremiah (m1). "Testamento" would read as a will.

source.text: ὁσάκις γὰρ ἐὰν ἐσθίητε τὸν ἄρτον τοῦτον καὶ τὸ ποτήριον πίνητε, τὸν θάνατον τοῦ κυρίου καταγγέλλετε, ἄχρι οὗ ἔλθῃ.

records.literal_gloss: As often as for you eat the bread this and the cup drink, the death of the Lord you proclaim, until which he comes.

en.L: For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the death of the Lord, until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes.
en.B: For each time you eat this bread and drink the cup, you are announcing the Lord's death, until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes.
en.R: Every time you eat this bread and drink from the cup, you are telling the news of the Lord's death. And you will keep doing so until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes again.

fr.L: Car toutes les fois que vous mangez ce pain et que vous buvez la coupe, vous proclamez la mort du Seigneur, jusqu’à ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vienne.
fr.B: Car chaque fois que vous mangez ce pain et que vous buvez la coupe, vous annoncez la mort du Seigneur, jusqu’à ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vienne.
